items.title: Nvidia earnings may come down to guidance and Jensen Huang's confidence
items.summary: Nvidia (NVDA) is just days away from releasing second quarter earnings results this Wednesday, August 26, as Wall Street expects quarterly revenue of $92 billion. The Morning Brief's Jake Conley sits down with Barron's senior markets analysis writer Paul La Monica and Infrastructure Capital Advisors CEO Jay Hatfield to discuss why excellent earnings may still not be enough to impress investors in this stage of the AI cycle.

items.title: AKAM Rides on Strength in Cloud Infrastructure Segment: Will It Last?
items.summary: Akamai's CIS segment increases 39% in Q2, fueled by AI workloads and GPU demand, but can its cloud infrastructure growth stay on track?

items.title: Microsoft Stock's Upside Now Runs Through Its Data Center Build
items.summary: The bull case here turns less on whether AI demand arrives than on how fast Microsoft can deliver the orders it has already booked.

items.summary: Nvidia Stock Falls as AI Server Prices Rise. Memory Costs Are to Blame

items.title: Workday to Report Q2 Earnings: Can Strong Revenues Drive Growth?
items.summary: WDAY's AI expansion is expected to support fiscal Q2 revenue growth, while higher costs, competition and cautious enterprise spending may pressure margins.

items.title: Nvidia Could Drop 20% On Poor Earnings
items.summary: Nvidia enters earnings week with its stock priced for perfection, but a single crack in its numbers could send investors scrambling for the exits. The question is whether any weakness even exists, and what happens if the market finds out the hard way.

items.title: Snowflake Stock Is Priced For Growth That Arrives At A Lower Gross Margin
items.summary: Snowflake's acceleration is led by AI products that carry a lower gross margin than its core platform, and a bandwidth-cost offset is what holds the margin guide together.

items.title: Nvidia raising AI server prices more than 15% amid memory costs
items.summary: The increases will apply to systems containing Vera Rubin and Grace Blackwell chips and take effect on shipments early next year
